newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices hold steady, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices hold steady, trade thin.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices held steady again Wednesday, helped by firmer crude, but trade remained thin amid still-mild East Coast weather and some fuel switching to cheaper natgas, industry sources said.

"The market feels pretty steady. There's not a whole lot of material showing, but it won't take much supply to kill it," said one cash trader, noting cheap gas and mild weather continued to cut utility fuel burns.
In New York Harbor, prompt one percent stayed at $18.50-75 a barrel, with October paper quoted 15-20 cents higher early at $18.70-90 but likely up even further with crude.
NYH high sulphurs also were little changed, with 2.2 percent still quoted at $17.00-17.25, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf Coast, prices also were steady, with one percent still at $16.75-17.00 and three percent at about $16.50.
Traders said 50,000 barrels of prompt USG 3.2 percent material (high viscosity, low gravity) sold at $16.30.
Mild weather in the U.S. Northeast pressured New York city gate swing gas prices down almost five cents to $2.05/mmBtu versus NYH one percent resid at a $2.96/mmBtu equivalent.
